summary: The video side is built as a scan-time pipeline. Background VRAM and character ROM are addressed straight from the H/V counters, and sprites go through a per-line RAM scan into a double line buffer, then a per-pixel priority mux and a palette PROM lookup. None of this follows MAME's tilemap/draw_sprites/screen_update batch structure. Against that, the sprite engine uses MAME's spriteram/spriteram_2/spriteram_3 names, and the custom I/O chip is a behavioural model whose credit and edge-detect logic follows namcoio_device::handle_coins and its mode switch on RAM[8]. Overall it leans toward hardware structure, with MAME-flavoured naming and an HLE of the I/O chip.

findings.signal: BG fetched per pixel from raster counters
findings.note: VRAM address, char ROM address {code,~HP[2],VP[2:0]} and the per-pixel bit pick (CHRO[7]/CHRO[3] ... selected by HP[1:0]) are all driven from HPOS/VPOS every VCLK. There is no tile cache or tilemap object.
SCROLL is captured into BGVSCR on each posedge of oHB and added to VPOS in the address adder. That is a raster-timed latch, not MAME's once-per-frame set_scrolly over columns 2..33.

findings.signal: Sprite line scan into double line buffer
findings.note: During active display the engine walks the 64 sprite slots for the next line, does a y-hit test with an adder plus size mask, then counts out 16/32 pixels into a ping-pong line buffer swapped on VPOS[0]. MAME instead draws whole sprites with gfx transmask in a frame batch with nested x/y tile loops and gfx_offs tables.
Visibility is y = spriteram_2 + 0x10 + vposl masked by a size-dependent mask and compared, the way a comparator/adder chain would do it. MAME's sy arithmetic is not reproduced.

findings.signal: Per-pixel priority mux and PROM palette
findings.mame_ref: mappy_v.cpp:screen_update_superpac / screen_update_mappy (two-pass tilemap draw by category)
findings.note: Priority is one combinational mux, BGHI ? BGCOL : (sprite==15 ? BGCOL : SPCOL), feeding a 32-byte palette PROM addressed {1,clut}/{0,sprite}. MAME redraws the tilemap a second time for category 1 instead.

findings.signal: Three parallel sprite RAMs read as one word
findings.note: Work RAM is three separate 2Kx8 dual-port RAMs. The video port reads all three at once as a 24-bit sprite word, like separate RAM chips on the video bus, rather than one shared region indexed by offsets.

findings.signal: MAME variable names in sprite engine
findings.note: The sprite RAM bytes are named spriteram, spriteram_2 and spriteram_3, which are exactly MAME's local pointer names, not board net names.

findings.signal: I/O chip modelled after namcoio HLE
findings.note: The custom I/O chip is a behavioural model, not a model of the actual MCU. It uses nibble RAM arrays, a credits register with credit_add/credit_sub (MAME's names), toggle-edge detection ((x^prev)&x, like val & toggled), BCD credit output, and mode chosen from RAM location 8 (IORAM_READ(8)), all updated once per VBLANK.

findings.signal: Tile scan mapping equals MAME mapper
findings.note: The address forms {COL[4:0],ROW[4:0]}/{ROW,COL} with ROW+2, and {1111,COL[1:0],ROW4,ROW[3:0]} for the fixed columns, encode the same mapping as MAME's mappers, including the +2 row offset. The hardware has to produce the same mapping, so this does not show provenance.

findings.signal: Control latches with A0 as data
findings.note: IRQ enables, sub-CPU reset, I/O reset and sound enable are each decoded from A[15:1] with A0 as the latch data, which is LS259 behaviour. MAME and the board share this, and it is coded as separate flops rather than as a 259 module.

findings.signal: Memory decode and linear HV timing
findings.note: Address decoding matches the shared memory map, and the H/V counters are a generic generator with jump points. Neither tells the two origins apart.
